title: Future Plans for Family Nexus Centres and Other Key Initiatives in Child and Maternal Health and Well-Being Taskforce Report
what_it_is: Future Plans for Family Nexus Centres and Other Key Initiatives in Child and Maternal Health and Well-Being Taskforce Report

sections.label: Health questions on Family Nexus
sections.summary: Questions ask about Family Nexus impact, community feedback, expansion plans, and measurable outcomes and evaluation of CAMH Taskforce initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what is the impact and utilisation of the Family Nexus sites established at Tampines, Punggol, Sembawang, and Choa Chu Kang; (b) what feedback has been received from the community; and (c) whether there are plans for expanding such sites to other regions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health with regard to the report from the interagency Child and Maternal Health and Well-being (CAMH) Taskforce published on 14 June 2024, what measurable outcomes have been observed from the 28 initiatives that have been implemented so far.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health how is the effectiveness of the key initiatives for the mental health screening and support for mothers, as provided in the report from the interagency Child and Maternal Health and Well-being (CAMH) Taskforce published on 14 June 2024, being evaluated.

sections.label: CAMH Taskforce report publication
sections.summary: The Child and Maternal Health and Well-being Taskforce published its Strategy and Action Plan report on 14 June 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The Child and Maternal Health and Well-being (CAMH) Taskforce published its Strategy and Action Plan report on 14 June 2024.

sections.label: CAMH initiative rollout status
sections.summary: Of the 48 initiatives, 28 have been rolled out and the remainder will be progressively implemented over the next two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Of the 48 initiatives, 28 have been rolled out and the remainder will be progressively implemented over the next two years.

sections.label: Project HOME and HEADS-UPP enrolment
sections.summary: As of mid-2024, Project HOME enrolled over 100 families in the North-East and HEADS-UPP onboarded 147 children in the West.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: As of mid-2024, Project HOME has enrolled more than 100 families in the North-East region, while HEADS-UPP has onboarded 147 children in the West.

sections.label: Family Nexus sites and referrals
sections.summary: Family Nexus has four sites; FamNex@Bukit Canberra drew over 1,500 participants, FamNex@OTH received over 380 referrals, and FamNex@Punggol referred over 500 cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Family Nexus brings together the health and social support services that families need.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We have so far introduced the Family Nexus initiative across four sites to improve coordination and make it easier for families to access the support they need.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: For instance, FamNex@Bukit Canberra has attracted more than 1,500 participants since it began operations in November 2023, reflecting a keen interest among parents and caregivers to engage in educational and wellness building activities with their children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: In terms of referrals, FamNex@OTH had received more than 380 cases from community nurses since its soft launch in November 2022, while FamNex@Punggol had referred more than 500 cases to social service agencies from December 2023 to May 2024.

sections.label: Question on seamless mother experience
sections.summary: A supplementary question asks how the task force will give mothers a more seamless experience, possibly through Health Hub.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: My supplementary questions are: firstly, with the many agencies across health, social and education involved in delivering over 40 initiatives, with 28 already implemented, how does the task force think that a mother who is coping with all the pregnancy demands and delivering her first baby would be able to have a more seamless experience, whether Health Hub maybe will be the digital platform that they can see all their case notes and intervention for coordination for their health?

sections.label: Community support and nurse training
sections.summary: Minister will consult HPB on using Community Health Points and notes community nurses need training for maternal and child issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: I agree that we can do more to help the community provide support as we scale up the support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: I will consult with HPB on how this can be done, whether the Community Health Points, for example, can be used as one of the areas where we can rally our community to come together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: But at the same time, our community nurses currently are only trained mostly for senior care, and we do need to train them to address maternal and child issues, which will also need a little time for us to keep up with.

sections.label: Hybrid Family Nexus configurations
sections.summary: Various hybrid configurations are being evaluated within two years, with rollout prioritised by mother-child dyad density once a pilot is proven.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Another one is where the polyclinic has a small unit onsite together with the social service agency, which is a hybrid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: So, we are still looking at the various hybrids and the various configurations and then evaluate within, say, two years to see what best, how best and what suits where, in terms of the impact that we can provide for our mother and child dyad.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: But for now, what we are looking at is what is the density of the mother-child dyad like and that will be our priority on when we will roll this out, when the pilot is proven and chosen in terms of whether it is a hybrid type, community type or polyclinic type.

sections.label: Antenatal postnatal mental wellness rollout
sections.summary: MP asks about plans to roll out antenatal and postnatal mental wellness support to other hospitals and consistency across public and private hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: My question surrounds the antenatal and postnatal mental wellness support which the Minister shared earlier that has been rolled out at KKH and NUH.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This supplementary question is in relation to whether there are plans to roll out to other hospitals, for example, like at the Singapore General Hospital (SGH), and also, in terms of the consistencies of the services to be provided by these public hospitals, are we ensuring that there is some level of consistency in terms of the practices that are being shared with the patients as compared to the private hospitals' patients in these aspects?

sections.label: Family Nexus and prenatal guidelines
sections.summary: Family Nexus centres will be rolled out earliest where young couples live, and prenatal mental health guidelines were launched in February last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: To answer the second question, yes, indeed, we look at the density of where young couples live and the potential for them to have children, have families, and those are actually where we would roll out the earliest next tranche of Family Nexus centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: On the issue of antenatal and postnatal care, the prenatal mental health guidelines for women of childbearing age were developed by KKH, together with the College of Obstetrics and Gynaecologists (OB/GYN) and have been launched in February last year and are already disseminated to healthcare professionals and the general public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: So, there is one for healthcare and there is one for the professionals; and there is a consensus statement published in the Annals of the Academy of Medicine, summary of the guidelines and they are all available on the KKH website.
